experiment: Linear-A-like degradation of frozen known-answer Linear B detector input

document_token_scale.method: seeded whole-document subset optimization minimizing absolute token-count error; no word-level sampling

recurrence_pressure.note: Do not alter Linear B word identities merely to force a vocabulary match.

damage_missingness.method: independent sign masking after document sampling; boundary and internal masks tracked separately
damage_missingness.fully_masked_handling: count explicitly as missing-word outcomes; exclude from detector-facing sequences but retain denominator diagnostics

frozen_detector_contract.source: scripts/run_damos_blind_calibration.py at the authenticated 2.3 baseline commit

reporting: positive positional screens and directed edge-removal relations
gold-supported recovery metrics only after gold scoring contract is available
interpretation_limits: Degradation sensitivity does not establish Linear A morphology.
Failure under degraded Linear B bounds detector sensitivity under sparse evidence; it does not disprove structure in Linear A.
Success under degraded Linear B establishes robustness only to modeled degradation factors.
No 2.4 performance result may be reported before the 2.3 gate is satisfied.
